findings.reason: the honest change is to add a network-fetch capability (oras single-layer blob pull) to the machine_artifact owner and have the validator lane resolve through `resolve_machine_artifact`, rather than stand up a parallel digest cache that will diverge from the one already tested in tests/test_mast_artifact.py.
findings.text: §3 proposes a new fetch module that pins OCI layer digests, verifies each blob's sha256, and materializes into a local cache root, but `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py` already owns exactly this: `materialize_machine_artifact`/`resolve_machine_artifact` (digest-addressed `sha256/<digest>` object root via `_verified_object_root`, line 862), `_sha256_bytes` verification, canonical cache-root resolution, and DD-version pinning through `pinned_dd_version`; a second verifier/cache forks the trust boundary and drifts on layout, digest checks and DD-pin semantics

findings.reason: naming the in-repo owners (machine_artifact for the pinned cache, pf_active/pf_passive for the IDS→coilset build) would let rungs 1 and 3 extend tested code instead of re-deriving it, which is the point of a prior-art search.
findings.text: the plan's reuse map names the norma corpus resolver (which lives outside nova; the referenced `nova.assembly.provenance.corpus` path does not exist in this tree) and imas-efit's tooling, but omits `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py` and `nova/imas/pf_active.py`/`pf_passive.py` (rung 3's "build the machine from the input bundle's own IDSs" re-derives coilset-from-IDS construction that already exists)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3 hides fetch-by-digest, sha256 verification, NC→HDF5 conversion, DD-pinned open and an availability gate behind one small module interface; the behaviour hidden is substantially larger than the interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the fetch/verify/cache-root mechanism §3 builds duplicates the content-addressed cache owner `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py`, which should be extended instead of forked.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites external precedents (the norma corpus resolver, imas-efit's comparator/CLI) and the availability-gate test, but never cites nova's own in-repo content-addressed OCI artifact machinery (`nova/imas/machine_artifact.py)`, which already implements the exact digest-pin + sha256-verify + local-cache-root mechanism §3 proposes to rebuild.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 gives the required justification for not reusing imas-efit's `efit pull` CLI (whole-bundle 286 MB vs ~16 MB of single layers fetched by digest), so the shim is justified rather than a bare parallel wrapper.
